1. Plan structure: kept the 10 sections and the front-matter keys; §3 split into 3.1–3.4 and §6 opened with the dependency mermaid so the plan carries the graph the assignment asked for without a new top-level section.
2. `recon/<path>` is described as the read-only sync of `$S/internal/breadth/<path>` (reference for each brief's §5 ports, never imported by `server/`, meter-number files excluded by the hygiene deny-list); the other snapshot directories stay untouched until Hunter decides (WS-00 D-01).
3. Group mapping: the README and templates use three groups (A = WS-00/01/02/03/11/12, B = WS-04/05/06/13, C = WS-07/08/09/10/14) as in `notes.md` and the coordinator's message; `seam-decisions.md` §9's "group B (WS-04…WS-10, WS-13, WS-14)" is read as B + C, and the README says so.
4. Mermaid: node ids without spaces, every label quoted, no `;` inside labels, braces kept out of labels; three diagrams in the plan (services, stage DAG, workstream graph) and one in the README; not rendered (no mermaid CLI on this VM), syntax checked by inspection and a script that scanned node ids and labels.
5. Version bumps: hosted-architecture v0 → v0.1 (new §5 change log); format doc v0 → "doc revision 0.1" (new §8); packet spec v0.4 → "doc revision 0.4.1" with `formatVersion` unchanged (WS-14 §4.3: descriptions and examples never bump the format version). The additive verdict field `view_angle_deg` and the `scale_source` value `meter_model` are optional, so every existing valid document stays valid.
6. Spec Appendix A was edited for the two queue items (`obliqueCloseUp.still`, `$id`) although it breaks byte-parity with the JSON copies until the WS-00/WS-14 spec PR updates them; the `compat` definition and the finalize/confirmations details went into Appendix D prose instead of the schema to keep the drift to those two paths (verified by diff).
7. The confirmations route in hosted-architecture and the spec follows SD-21 (`{fieldId, kind, value?, imageId, clientAt}`), not WS-08's original `{stillId, choice, typed}` proposal.
8. Monthly VLM cost rows in hosted-architecture §1 are derived arithmetic ($0.30 × 3,000 and × 30,000) and are labelled as such; every other number in the four documents is copied from a measured source with the source named.
9. Decidability gets no floor: the README/plan report it per site with the E2E baseline and forbid a PR from lowering it on a golden site, until Base sets a review-rate target (the queue asked for a "decidability floor" gate; without a Base target a hard floor would be invented).
10. The README carries the `cursor.subagentId` frontmatter (as `docs/hosted-architecture.md` and `docs/gate-decision.md` do); the plan, spec and format doc keep their existing headers.

## 5. Decisions for Hunter to confirm (the defaults builders assume)

1. Photo flow runs inside the app so every photo and both meter close-ups carry an ARKit pose; camera-roll import stays the lowest tier (`photo_only`). Default assumed yes.
2. Toolchain: `pycolmap==4.2.0` with a matching COLMAP CUDA rebuild (parity with the measured A1/A6 recipe; ~609 s clean compile, prebuilt and pinned by WS-12) unless WS-04 proves the 3.11.1 image reproduces A6 within tolerance. Default 4.2.0.
3. GCP bootstrap: create `house-scanning`, link billing, enable APIs, run the first `terraform apply` locally, set the GitHub variables and Modal Secrets; PR S on the SMP repo (or apply its diff by hand). Default until then: `STORAGE_BACKEND=volume`, WS-12 fallback (own pool + `hss-tfstate`).
4. Modal dashboard: $200 workspace spend limit, `dev` $140 / `prod` $60 environment budgets, `dev` and `prod` environments, Secrets `hss-<env>-vlm/api/gcp` by name.
5. GitHub app access for builders on the server repo and the SMP repo. Default: Mac-sync pushes, PRs opened by Hunter.
6. Capture day: two houses (R1 expected pass under A and C, R2 expected reject), one non-Pro and one LiDAR iPhone, the iOS v0.4 app build. Default: fallbacks; R2 pending if only one house.
7. Labels: approve the v0.5 → v0.6 rulings and the blind R1/R2 labels. Default: draft, still scored.
8. ETH3D-derived small JSON (GT scenes, verdicts, labels, manifests) committed to the private repo with licence notes. Default yes.
9. Bucket naming `hss-captures-<env>` (vs SMP's `house-scanning-<env>-captures`). Default `hss-`.
10. Base's answers to relay: rule set C for Texas; homeowner never sees `reject`; ground rule `angle80` with `footprint3in` for the positive-pass gate; photos may go to OpenAI/xAI in dev (explicit in prod); an unconfirmed meter number forces review; photo facts never auto-pass (rule proposed: pass when GPT-5.5 and Grok 4.7 agree, no hazard flag, brand not on the recall list); battery height 39.5 in; placeholder numbers (headroom, slope, step, sill, backing); meter dimension table calipers (~15 models); packet retention; IdP JWT parameters; which identifier on multi-identifier plates.
